## Amon-Ra St. Brown

His usage is elite, but the production has slipped. He averages 10.9 targets a game on a 31% share and 84% of snaps. Over the last 4 games that is 10.3 targets, a 30% share, 83% of snaps and 7 red-zone targets (1.8 a game). He also has 16 red-zone targets and 5 goal-line targets on the season. He is scoring less than that volume suggests. He is at 16.4 half-PPR points a game over 7 games, and 12.5 over the last 4 with no touchdowns. His 7.5 yards per target is low for a player this heavily targeted.

The ribs are the main concern. He is Questionable and was limited Wednesday and Thursday. Rib injuries (bruised or cracked ribs) usually don't cost a receiver games. The risk is that a hard hit in-game re-aggravates it. A limited Thursday practice with a Friday decision still pending means he likely plays, but he may be less than 100%, and a game-day scratch is possible. My searches found nothing newer than the Thursday report. Check the final status Sunday morning.

On the Lions' receiver depth, Jameson Williams has an 18% share and 7 red-zone targets over the last 4 games, so he soaks up real work. Isaac TeSlaa is at 10%. St. Brown's volume is safe, but the offense isn't producing much through him.

The matchup is poor. Miami is the 3rd toughest WR matchup (×0.90), and the injury discount (×0.85) puts his Week 9 projection at 10.8 with a 7.6 floor and 17.5 ceiling. His rest-of-season projection is 133.4, on a schedule rated 0.99, which is roughly average.

## Jaxon Smith-Njigba

He is the better player right now by a wide margin. He averages 23.5 points a game over 8 games, with 188.0 total, 36% target share and 85% of snaps. Over the last 4 games he has 11.8 targets a game, a 35% share, 88% of snaps and 126.0 receiving yards a game. He has also averaged 11.1 yards per target all season and has 9 touchdowns. Beyond his receiving, he has 3.6 rushing yards a game on 9.7 yards per carry. His red-zone work is modest (3 red-zone targets in the last 4 games, no goal-line targets), so some of his touchdown total may not repeat. His yardage base is large enough that this matters little.

He has no injury listed. The teammate news adds to his value. Rashid Shaheed (knee) sat out Monday, and the Fantasy Footballers report that he is iffy for Week 9. The coach said he has a chance to play but may need a full practice to do it. Shaheed has a 15% share over the last 4 games, so if he is out, much of that volume should go to Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp (13%) and Tory Horton (11%).

The matchup is good. Arizona is the 8th easiest WR matchup (×1.05), the game is at home, and his Week 9 projection is 23.7 with a 17.8 floor and 30.5 ceiling. His rest-of-season projection is 187.4 on a schedule rated 1.02.

## The verdict

Smith-Njigba is the pick for both Week 9 and the rest of the season. His 23.7-point projection is more than double St. Brown's 10.8. His floor of 17.8 is higher than St. Brown's ceiling of 17.5, and he has the healthier status and the better matchup.

St. Brown's ceiling should recover over time. Lions volume this heavy tends to regress toward touchdowns, and the 5 goal-line targets show he is still used near the end zone. In the short term, though, the rib injury and the Miami matchup make him a risky play. If you have a better option, bench him this week. If you don't, he is still a start at that volume. Before you rely on him, check his Sunday status.

Hold both if you own them. Don't trade Smith-Njigba away for St. Brown unless you are getting a lot back.
